subject: Executive sponsor recap: infrastructure constraints, SLOs, and procurement path
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@thermacrest.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Executive sponsor recap: infra constraints, SLOs, and procurement path

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we captured the sponsor priorities and to surface the procurement path we discussed. Notes below are aligned to the exec call and to the infra/ops folks you flagged.

Top business outcomes (sponsor-level):
- Reduce inference cost per 1M requests by ~30–50% within pilot (target: 40%), while maintaining output fidelity for customer-facing features.
- Stabilize tail latency so 99th percentile < 250ms for interactive flows; SLO target 99.9% availability for inference endpoints.
- Ensure data residency for EU customer segments and controls for PHI-analogous telemetry.

Key pain points you emphasized:
- Latency spikes during end-of-month reporting windows; observed token bursts cause timeouts upstream.
- Lack of predictable unit economics across different models and traffic profiles.
- Procurement/legal need SOC 2 evidence + a clear operational runbook before a PO can be issued.

Technical constraints / ops blockers:
- Firewalled VPC with strict egress rules — may require inbound NAT or allow-listing of Redwood inference nodes.
- Preference for Reserved/Dedicated capacity for production to satisfy throughput SLAs.
- On-prem appliance considered for EU-regulated workloads; we need details on network topology and A/V constraints.

Proposed pilot and procurement path (next steps we recommend):
1) Pilot scope: 4-week dedicated pilot (non-prod -> prod pilot step) focusing on 3 high-traffic endpoints, baseline metrics collection, and 2-week load-ramp. Owner: Redwood (Karthik). Target start: week of 09/28.
2) Security evidence: we attached a Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf and a one-page runbook template for your security review. Owner: Kimberly (deliverables by 09/17).
3) Commercial: 60-day evaluation credit + discounted reserved pricing for first 6 months; we can share a draft SOW for your procurement/legal. Owner: Kimberly, commercial draft in this thread.
4) Legal/contract: we will accept standard ThermaCrest redlines on data transfer and liability; propose DocuSign flow after procurement and security sign-off.

Escalation items (sponsor asks):
- If SOC 2 artifacts do not satisfy internal auditors, elevate to Redwood security leadership (Vivek) to arrange a private review.
- If network allow-listing is not possible, plan fallback to a dedicated VPC peering + NAT gateway approach.

Open assumptions to confirm:
- ThermaCrest procurement can approve a pilot PO within 2–3 weeks of receiving the SOW.
- Legal will need a 2–3 business day turnaround on minor T&Cs once the SOW is accepted.

Next calls proposed:
- Procurement + legal + infra working session (30m) — proposed 09/16 or 09/17.
- Technical kickoff for pilot (60m) — proposed 09/29.

Please review and flag any corrections. If this aligns, I will route the SOW draft and SOC2 summary to Procurement and Legal and schedule the working session.

Thanks again — look forward to partnering on the pilot.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf (summary), Initial-SOW-ThermaCrest-v0.2.docx (draft)

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@thermacrest.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: ThermaCrest Procurement <procurement@thermacrest.com>, Alyssa Gomez <alyssa.gomez@thermacrest.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Executive sponsor recap: infra constraints, SLOs, and procurement path

Kimberly —

Appreciate the thorough summary, that aligns with what the execs want to see. A few quick items from our side:

- Procurement: we received the sample commercial terms earlier; procurement will need the SOW + itemized pricing to generate a PO. I'll ask procurement to prioritize a 48–72 hour turnaround after they get the final SOW.
- Security: Alyssa will validate the SOC 2 summary; if she needs the full report we can arrange an NDA. Please include contact info for Redwood's security lead.
- Network: our infra team confirmed they prefer allow-listing but will accept the dedicated VPC peering fallback. They asked for IP ranges and an expected egress profile to confirm bandwidth cost assumptions.

I'll coordinate on dates for 09/16 for a procurement/infra sync. Please send the SOW and the SOC 2 summary to procurement@thermacrest.com and alyssa.gomez@thermacrest.com.

One more ask from the sponsor: can Redwood commit to a mid-pilot checkpoint with executive readout (30m) to validate value? Sponsor wants a business-metrics update at week 3.

Sanjay
VP Product, ThermaCrest

On attachments: we attached ThermaCrest-Procurement-Checklist.xlsx to procurement; expect comments on standard PO template.

From: ThermaCrest Procurement <procurement@thermacrest.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@thermacrest.com>
Cc: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa.gomez@thermacrest.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Executive sponsor recap: infra constraints, SLOs, and procurement path

Kimberly —

Procurement has access to the Procurement Checklist and has started mapping internal approval gates. A few timeline notes:

- PO approval (pilot): procurement lead expects to issue a pilot PO within 10 business days of receiving the final SOW and itemized cost.
- Invoicing: procurement needs billing address and remittance details to be included in the SOW.
- Contracting: standard term edits are acceptable; we will surface any high-risk clauses during review.

Please send the SOW and remittance info to procurement@thermacrest.com. We will set up a short 30m review meeting after we get the SOW to walk through invoicing and lead times.

Thanks —
ThermaCrest Procurement Team
procurement@thermacrest.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@thermacrest.com>, ThermaCrest Procurement <procurement@thermacrest.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Executive sponsor recap: infra constraints, SLOs, and procurement path

Thanks team — noted and will do. Quick commitments and calendar actions from Redwood: 

- Deliverables: I will send the SOW (Initial-SOW-ThermaCrest-v0.2.docx) and Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf to procurement@thermacrest.com and alyssa.gomez@thermacrest.com by EOD 09/15.
- Security lead: Vivek Kulkarni (vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com) will be available for any security callbacks / NDA discussions.
- Pilot kickoff: targeting 09/29; I will drop a calendar hold for a 60m technical kickoff this afternoon for 09/29 and a 30m procurement/infra working session for 09/16 at 10:00 AM PT — please accept or propose alternate times.
- Mid-pilot exec checkpoint: we commit to a week-3 30m readout and will prepare a 1-page business metrics slide for the sponsor.

Action items (owners):
- Kimberly: send SOW, SOC2 summary, remittance details (EOD 09/15).
- Karthik: prepare pilot runbook and expected IP ranges/egress profile (due 09/24).
- Vivek: standby for security callbacks / NDA (as needed).

If that works I will proceed with the DocuSign draft once procurement confirms PO timing.

Best,
Kim
